- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67) followed by a sharp drop, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment change is negative and recent, model often underreacts — adjust forecast upward by 3–8% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- In high-news-volume periods, model tends to overfit short-term volatility — dampen forecast variance by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction of 1–3% per day to reflect mean reversion.
- When sentiment is flat or negative for 3+ days, model often fails to recognize bearish trend — reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment decay.
- For spikes in sentiment (e.g., >0.8), model often overestimates price rise — cap forecast at +10% above recent high, then apply 1–2% decay per day.
- If sentiment change is erratic (e.g., ±0.5+ in 2 consecutive days), model overfits — use sentiment median instead of mean for forecasting.
